title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 52 (Application of Premiums Received on Issue of Shares)

content.overview: Section 52 requires that where a company issues shares at a premium, whether for cash or otherwise, a sum equal to the aggregate amount or value of the premiums on those shares be transferred to a securities premium account. The section restricts the application of that account to specified purposes such as issuing fully paid bonus shares, writing off preliminary expenses, writing off expenses of issue or commission/discount on issue of shares or debentures, providing for premium payable on redemption of preference shares or debentures, and buy-back under section 68.
content.glance: Premiums go to securities premium account; application limited to statutory purposes (bonus shares, write-offs, redemption premium, buy-back).
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 52 (Application of premiums received on issue of shares). Where a company issues shares at a premium, whether for cash or otherwise, the aggregate amount/value of the premium must be transferred to a securities premium account. The account may be applied only to the purposes permitted by the section, including issuing fully paid bonus shares; writing off preliminary expenses; writing off expenses of, or commission/discount allowed on, an issue of shares or debentures; providing for premium payable on redemption of redeemable preference shares or debentures; and buying back its own shares or other securities under section 68. Subsection (3) allows specified classes of companies that meet the prescribed accounting-standard conditions to use the account for the listed purposes in that subsection. Securities premium is not a free reserve for ordinary dividend or unrestricted use. Verify the applicable company-class conditions and current accounting rules before relying on subsection (3).

sections.heading: Transfer of premium
sections.body: When shares are issued at a premium, whether for cash or otherwise, the aggregate amount/value of that premium must be transferred to the securities premium account.

sections.heading: Permitted applications
sections.body: The section permits specified uses, including fully paid bonus shares, writing off preliminary expenses, writing off issue expenses/commission/discount, providing for redemption premium on preference shares or debentures, and buy-back under section 68.

sections.heading: Prescribed class of companies
sections.body: Subsection (3) permits specified classes of companies that meet the prescribed accounting-standard conditions to use the account for the purposes listed in that subsection. Verify the current class and accounting conditions.

sections.heading: Restriction
sections.body: The account is not a free reserve for ordinary dividend or unrestricted use; the proposed application must fit a statutory purpose.

provisions.title: Application of premiums received on issue of shares

examples.title: Bonus from premium
examples.body: The company issues fully paid bonus shares by capitalising the securities premium account. Section 52 permits this application.

examples.title: Impermissible use
examples.body: The company tries to distribute securities premium as ordinary dividend. Section 52 does not permit that application.

hypotheticals.question: Can securities premium be used to pay ordinary dividends?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 52 limits application to the listed purposes; ordinary dividend is not among them.

distinctions.title: Securities premium and discount prohibition
distinctions.left: Section 52 governs receipt and permitted application of share premium.
distinctions.right: Section 53 prohibits discounted share issues, subject to its statutory exceptions.

rows.left: Above nominal value; premium is recorded

misconceptions.trap: Securities premium is free reserves available for any purpose.
misconceptions.correction: Section 52 restricts application to specified purposes only.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can securities premium be used to pay an ordinary dividend?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Section 52 restricts its application to specified statutory purposes.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does subsection (3) apply identically to every company?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. It is limited to prescribed classes of companies whose financial statements meet the prescribed accounting-standard conditions.
